cve_summary: Race condition in the scan_get_next_rmap_item function in mm/ksm.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.39.3, when Kernel SamePage Merging (KSM) is enabled, allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted application.
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Retrieves the next rmap_item from a specified page in the kernel's memory management system.

Parameters: 
page (struct page **): A pointer to a pointer that will hold the address of the retrieved page.

Returns: 
struct rmap_item *: A pointer to the next rmap_item if found, or NULL if no more items are available.

Logic: 
The function first checks if the list of memory management structures is empty. If not, it retrieves the next mm_slot and scans through the virtual memory areas (VMAs) of the associated memory structure. It looks for VMAs marked as mergeable and retrieves pages accordingly. If a valid page is found, it processes it to obtain the corresponding rmap_item. If no mergeable VMAs are found, it cleans up the current mm_slot and prepares for the next iteration. The function continues scanning until all items have been processed or no more items are available.
"""
